The black hand c covers a grey machine impression with a right upright, upper curve and right foot. It is a-like but fused with the retracing; a/c remains qualified rather than replaced by a clean c. A normal c/e impression elsewhere was compared directly.
The added word is typed above des variétés, starting near the end of Hodge; all its accents are visible. A pen line rises from the Hodge/des gap, runs below the word and curls up at the right.
A separate horizontal stroke is directly below the single typed C; there is no double-stem alphabet.
The comma at the end of complexes is covered by a compact black cancellation. Its downward original tail remains visible below the crossing ink. H gives it live.
The added words are on a raised typed line over the end of justifie and par voie. A curved pen underline curls at both ends and has a descending attachment after justifie.

At the clipped right edge there is dark hand ink descending after the last letter, with a comma-like lower turn; the end of the retraced m and a lower grey/brown blot cannot be separated completely. A mark is retained, qualified as comma rather than silently omitted or assigned an additional letter.
The machine letters read c-o-h-o-m-o-l-i-g-u-e. The expected o/q sequence is not on the page and is not supplied.

changes.place: en caractéristique nulle and live old words
changes.shows: The new phrase is typed above des variétés algébriques. Its enclosing pen outline is open along the upper middle, runs across the tops of the old type, and drops after algébriques; the old words are live, with no x row or independent cancellation. The insertion belongs after them. H moves it before them and wrongly cancels them.

Typed semble begins slightly to the left above cancelled est. The old letters have both typewriter crosses and a pen line; a curved leader rises from the right of the old word toward the right of the addition.

After alg, a typed b ascender/left serif survives under handwritten é with its loop/bar and acute. The next cell has an é-like old impression and acute beside the new b but is fused enough to retain é/b. In the third, old u/r remains under the compressed handwritten ri, including a separate dot before the typed q. The three superpositions are recorded without asserting their chronological order.
Between typed qu and es, an extra p has its own bowl, descender and lower foot beneath an x. Both witnesses omit this cancelled letter.
A distinct short rising diagonal stands above the cancelled e and below the r of raised preuve. The acute is separate from both words and resolves C’s accent doubt.
The replacement is typed directly above the beginning of résolution, sharing its left edge. No separate leader is visible.
After signaler and a space, a further c survives under x: an upper-right terminal, curved left side and lower return. Both drafts omit this abandoned letter.

The hand e overlaps an old type impression compatible with s, but its original curves cannot be fully separated. The following s is also handwritten. C’s old-letter doubt is retained and the overlap restored; H drops the old impression.

The new typed phrase stands above donnant en particulier, beginning slightly before the old d. The pen leader rises from the right of cancelled donnant and runs beneath the new words, curling on the right. H reverses their serial order and neither draft reproduces this relative level and line.
The Q has a separate underline; its hand-modified ell is lower and to the right. No second Q stem occurs.

Inside the heavy handwritten d, a grey machine e keeps an independent horizontal middlebar and upper bowl. The new d supplies the tall right ascender and broad oval. The old impression omitted by both is retained beneath it.

changes.C: inline insertion after cancelled se placent
changes.shows: The typed addition begins above et de niveau, well to the left of cancelled se placent. Its pen underline has a left curl, descends between niveau and the old phrase, rises again and curls at the right. Relative placement and attachment are retained.

After typed ad, the hand i/q/u/e cover four old cells, while final s remains typed. The first old cell has tall stem/serifs and a possible bowl (d/l); the second has an e bar/counter and possible acute (é/e); the third has a separate i dot and narrow upright; the fourth retains only an upper curve/left projection (a/p). Fused cells stay qualified instead of being restored from the expected word.
The first possible s is merged with the pen loop and x row, so C’s alternative remains. After déjà, an independent comma tail descends below the final cancellation stroke; both witnesses omit it.

The first e has a middlebar/open lower bowl; the following t has an ascender, crossbar and lower hook. qui follows in separate cells. The D is full height with a vertical left and right bowl. C reverses the first pair and lowers D; H leaves readable et qui as ill.
After the live Cet, a second t has its own ascender/crossbar under x and is followed by an e with a surviving upper counter and bar. C doubt is resolved; H drops both the live t and the cancelled te.

changes.place: point de vue addition and leader
changes.shows: The entire typed phrase is above old et qui Dans la and the theory line. A long pen line runs beneath it, curls/drops at the left, branches down between old la and théorie and curls around the right end. Its raised position is reproduced rather than treating it as ordinary baseline prose.
The cancellation crosses all three cells heavily. Parts compatible with c/a/r remain, but do not make the full old word independently certain. C’s qualification remains; H gives it without doubt.
Each opening and closing pair consists of two short high typewriter strokes. None has the angular shape of guillemets.
The p has a narrow descending stem beneath its rounded upper part, separate from the preceding e. C’s table resolution is independently confirmed; ceendant is rejected.
The entire phrase remains readable under the row of typed x, including capital P and the full ending introduction. No omitted continuation is supplied.
Each l-like type cell has an added diagonal handwritten stroke. Four body/coefficient occurrences and the raised addition were inspected; the coefficient sign is lowered.
Two pen square brackets enclose blank paper. The following parenthesis and period belong to the surrounding typed sentence.
Both standart endings have t stems/crossbars, niveau has no final x, and motivique has a separate descending comma. The unexpected forms and punctuation remain.
Separate pen lines underline each of the three words. The intervening des has a cancellation through its letters and is retained.
A separate pen point follows rationnels. A continuous horizontal pen stroke cancels the opening parenthesis and words; the final t reaches the right edge, and no closing parenthesis is visible.
